doc.title: Ruth Brisbane interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 2, 2013

title: Subway home after late nights
summary: Taking the A train home to Brooklyn at night, helped by Diahann Carroll's father.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: And how would you get home after that?

Believe it or not I’m amazed when I worked in Manhattan, all the way up to 125th, I took the subway home. I can’t imagine doing that today, or twenty years ago I couldn’t imagine doing that. And I had six blocks to walk from the subway in Brooklyn. I remember falling asleep on the train one night and Diahann Carroll’s father woke me up. He was a conductor on the A train, and that’s the train I took home to Brooklyn. And he woke me up and he said, “I believe you get off soon.” I will thank that man forever. Because I would never went past my stop which was Utica Avenue in Brooklyn, and I really would have been upset, more than upset. But my mother used to say if you ever feel that you have to take a cab home, even if you don’t have the money, we’ll find the money in the house somewhere to pay the cab driver.
Yeah, so those are some pretty late nights and you can watch the sun come up almost.
